hypothesis: A causally observed burst of forced BTC short-liquidation buying may contain incremental information about near-term bullish continuation after conditioning on post-burst price and book persistence, but an exhaustion reversal is an equally plausible competing mechanism and no directional edge is currently established.
decision: Retain only as a source-qualification candidate. Do not specify entry thresholds, inspect economic outcomes, acquire requester-pays data, or change V58 until explicit liquidation metadata, causal timestamps, declared-window completeness, acquisition cost, and operational isolation are validated.
recommendation: Qualify source completeness and economic acquisition feasibility before specifying or testing a strategy. Do not infer liquidation status from ordinary public trades, do not use user addresses as a predictive feature, do not inspect candidate outcomes before a separate exact preregistration, and do not change V58.
why_now: V58 has a confirmed BTC continuation-long coverage gap, while the already-opened price breakout, sweep relaxation, Hulk inversion, spot-lead, funding, pullback, order-flow absorption, bid-replenishment, OI, issuer-flow, options-volatility, and mark-oracle families have negative, non-distinct, or causally incomplete dispositions. Liquidation metadata is a materially different causal input if it can be acquired completely.
evidence_reviewed: The active V58 configuration has two BTC short-only Hulk providers and one sparse hourly sweep-reclaim long provider.
The 2026-08-22T00:35:42Z live checkpoint contained 25 BTC sweep-long evaluations, zero eligible signals, zero BTC router intents, zero withheld BTC intents, and zero BTC faults.
The frozen BTC-long frontier rejects or defers all enumerated prior candidate families and requires a materially new causal source or mechanism.

The prospective public BTC recorder accumulated 725 L2 snapshots, 25144 public trades, and 3809 asset-context rows over approximately 64.9 minutes after the frozen 2026-08-21T23:33:51Z frontier cutoff.
The existing public-trade parquet and 0xArchive trade schemas contain participant and aggressor evidence but no liquidation classification.
Hyperliquid official WebSocket documentation defines an optional liquidation object on user-fill records, while the ordinary public WsTrade schema has no liquidation field.
Hyperliquid official historical-data documentation identifies requester-pays node_fills_by_block data and states that node_fills matches the API fill format.
A read-only public liquidatable info query at approximately 2026-08-22T00:41Z succeeded and returned an empty array; this proves endpoint availability only, not historical or event completeness.
This host has no configured AWS access key, secret, session token, profile, AWS CLI, or boto3 client for requester-pays qualification.

observed_problem_or_opportunity.problem: Ordinary BTC bullish continuation is not covered by V58, and current public-trade evidence cannot distinguish forced liquidation fills from voluntary aggressive buys.
observed_problem_or_opportunity.opportunity: Explicit liquidation metadata may separate a new forced-flow mechanism from previously rejected generic flow and breakout candidates.

applicable_market_regime: Potential BTC bullish impulse during or immediately after forced short-liquidation flow; exact regime, onset, persistence, and exit conditions remain intentionally unspecified until source qualification succeeds.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Infer liquidations from large public buy trades
alternatives_considered.reason: Trade size and aggressor side do not establish liquidation causality.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Poll the current liquidatable endpoint as the primary event source
alternatives_considered.reason: A current-state snapshot can be empty and may miss short-lived liquidation execution; completeness and historical replay are unproven.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Run a local Hyperliquid non-validating node with fill output
alternatives_considered.reason: Official guidance describes substantial compute, memory, storage, and approximately 100 GB per day of default logs.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Qualify a bounded official requester-pays node-fill interval
alternatives_considered.reason: It is the lowest-complexity path to verify whether BTC fill rows retain causal liquidation metadata before any strategy contract is frozen.

expected_upside: If the source is complete and the later preregistered mechanism survives independent after-cost testing, it could add BTC continuation coverage using forced-flow information absent from current V58 inputs.
main_risks_and_failure_modes: Short-liquidation bursts may mark exhaustion and reversal rather than continuation.
Node-fill history may be delayed, incomplete, expensive, or omit enough metadata to prevent causal classification.
Historical BTC price outcomes have already been opened by other research, creating selection-bias risk even if liquidation metadata is newly acquired.
A rare-event feature may fail minimum cadence or be dominated by one cascade.
Polling or node operation could consume public-rate or host resources needed by the live system and therefore must remain isolated from V58.
validation_completed: Provider-map and router diagnosis, prior-family inventory, public-event recorder continuity measurement, existing trade-schema inspection, official-interface semantic review, and a credentials-presence preflight. No candidate outcomes were calculated.
validation_still_required: Obtain explicit authorization for any requester-pays acquisition after the operator accepts possible external transfer charges.
Acquire one small immutable official node-fill bundle and verify hashes, row ordering, timestamps, duplicate identities, side semantics, liquidation-field coverage, and BTC filtering.
Estimate full chronological coverage, bytes, cost, gaps, and liquidation-event cadence before widening acquisition.
Freeze a separate exact continuation hypothesis plus exhaustion placebo before opening economic outcomes.
Use realistic fees, funding, BBO depth, mark stops, latency, delay and slippage stress, chronological validation, untouched prospective evidence, largest-winner removal, and shared-V58 competition.
success_metrics: Source qualification is successful only if liquidation classification is explicit, causally timestamped, deduplicated, source-complete for declared bounds, and economically feasible to acquire. A later strategy is eligible for recommendation only if it is positive after costs in validation and independent evidence, positive excluding its largest winner, survives delay/slippage stress, has practical cadence, and improves the unchanged V58 shared portfolio.
failure_or_rollback_triggers: Close the data hypothesis if official samples omit liquidation classification, declared intervals cannot be proven complete, acquisition cost or operational isolation is unacceptable, or the source cannot be joined causally. Reject any later strategy without nearby retuning if either chronological out-of-sample partition, largest-winner removal, stress replay, or shared-portfolio comparison fails its preregistered threshold.
falsifier: Invalidate the source assessment if an official bounded sample proves that node fills do not retain explicit liquidation metadata or cannot establish causal event time and side. Update the mechanism assessment only after a preregistered independent test distinguishes continuation from exhaustion after all modeled costs.
single_highest_value_next_investigation: Resolve the currently open ETH and SP500 lifecycles against their preregistered exit and profit-protection challengers. In parallel, keep the BTC public recorder running; liquidation-source qualification remains queued until requester-pays access is explicitly authorized and available.
explicit_approval_requested: Approval would be required before incurring requester-pays archive transfer charges; no live-strategy approval is requested.

limitations: No official node-fill sample has yet verified usable liquidation-field coverage.
The public liquidatable endpoint returned no rows in one snapshot and does not establish historical completeness.
Historical BTC price outcomes have already been opened by prior research.
Continuation and exhaustion are competing mechanisms, and neither has outcome evidence here.
Requester-pays acquisition may incur external charges and has not been authorized or configured.
This record cannot pause, retune, route, size, enter, close, or promote any live strategy or lifecycle.
